findings.title: Accrued operator fees are counted in totalAssets, inflating the share price between harvest and fee collection
findings.exploit: Before a harvest, unclaimed rewards enter totalAssets net of the fee via getTotalRewards() (lines 276-285). harvest() moves the full reward into the vault as WRON and records operatorFeeAmount += reward * fee (line 137), but totalAssets() (line 294) uses super.totalAssets(), the raw WRON balance, which still contains the fee owed to feeRecipient. harvestAndDelegateRewards() does the same with the fee portion now counted inside getTotalStaked(). So totalAssets jumps by reward * fee at every harvest and only falls back when fetchOperatorFee() runs. An attacker deposits immediately before an operator harvest (or simply holds shares), then redeems or withdraws after it and before the fee is fetched, receiving assets priced on the inflated total. Every redemption in that window pays out part of the fee; when fetchOperatorFee() later withdraws operatorFeeAmount from the vault balance, the shortfall comes from the remaining depositors.
findings.impact: Remaining LRON holders pay the operator fee a second time on value already distributed to exiting or sandwiching users; if liquid WRON is thin, fetchOperatorFee or queued withdrawals revert.
findings.fix: Subtract operatorFeeAmount in totalAssets() (return super.totalAssets() + getTotalStaked() + getTotalRewards() - operatorFeeAmount), or transfer the fee to feeRecipient or a separate escrow at harvest time so it never sits in the vault's asset balance.
